features.title: Behavioral test baseline
features.summary: Protect the current user-list contract with deterministic browser tests that never call the live DummyJSON API.

in: Loading, successful response, request error, and empty response states
Required user-card fields
Case-insensitive full-name search after the 500 millisecond debounce
No-match search state
Mocked network responses for deterministic tests

acceptance_criteria: Tests distinguish loading, result, request error, empty response, and no-match states.
Tests verify that a result card displays image, full name, age, email, and phone.
Tests verify that search is case-insensitive, matches the combined first and last name, and waits for the 500 millisecond debounce.
Every fetch used by the test suite is mocked and no test calls DummyJSON.
npm run verify passes.

scope_approval.notes: The repository owner explicitly approved implementation and waived the grill-me interview because this feature codifies the existing product contract in tests.

features.title: GitHub CI/CD and Pages deployment
features.summary: Run reproducible lint, test, and production-build checks for pull requests and automatically deploy successful main builds to GitHub Pages.

in: GitHub Actions workflow for pull requests and pushes to main
Lockfile-based dependency installation
Dedicated React ESLint command
Non-interactive behavioral tests
Production build verification
Portable Create React App asset paths for a repository Pages URL
Automatic GitHub Pages deployment after a successful push to main
Documentation for required checks and the manual branch-ruleset step
out: Deployment to hosting providers other than GitHub Pages
Stored deployment credentials or production secrets

acceptance_criteria: A pull request targeting main automatically runs lint, tests, and a production build on a GitHub-hosted runner.
A push to main runs the same verification workflow.
CI installs dependencies with npm ci and does not make live DummyJSON requests during tests.
The lint command reports React and JavaScript lint failures non-interactively.
The production build uses asset paths that work under the customer_hook GitHub Pages repository path.
A successful push to main uploads the production build and deploys it to the github-pages environment.
The workflow uses least-privilege permissions and does not expose deployment secrets to pull requests.
Repository documentation explains the CI commands, one-time Pages setup, deployment behavior, and the GitHub ruleset setting required to block merging when CI fails.

scope_approval.notes: The repository owner selected GitHub Pages and approved pull-request verification plus automatic deployment after successful pushes to main.

features.title: Product metadata and configuration hygiene
features.summary: Replace template metadata, centralize build-time configuration, remove unused CRA starter files, and make the current toolchain more reproducible without migrating away from Create React App.

in: Customer Hook title, description, and web-app manifest metadata
Documented REACT_APP_USERS_API_URL configuration with a safe DummyJSON default
Named search debounce constant
Removal of reportWebVitals, web-vitals, and unused CRA logo source
Separation of browser runtime and development-only dependencies
Node.js and npm version metadata
Prettier format-check command in local verification and CI
Husky and lint-staged pre-commit checks for staged source and configuration
out: Retry controls or new product features

acceptance_criteria: Browser title, description, and installable-app manifest identify Customer Hook rather than React App or Create React App Sample.
The users endpoint reads REACT_APP_USERS_API_URL at build time and safely defaults to https://dummyjson.com/users.
The 500 millisecond search debounce is referenced through a named configuration constant.
reportWebVitals.js, logo.svg, and the direct web-vitals dependency are removed without changing application behavior.
Only React browser runtime packages remain in dependencies; build and test packages are in devDependencies.
package.json records Node.js >=22.22.1, npm 10.x, and npm@10.9.4, while CI uses Node.js 22.22.1.
npm run format:check is documented and enforced by npm run verify and the GitHub Quality gate.
npm ci prepares a Husky pre-commit hook that runs non-mutating ESLint and Prettier checks only against applicable staged files.
All five existing behavioral tests pass and the production build retains repository-relative asset paths.

scope_approval.notes: The repository owner explicitly selected this bounded hygiene work and asked for implementation on a dedicated branch while deferring Vite.

features.title: Migrate from Create React App to Vite
features.summary: Replace the Create React App toolchain with Vite in a dedicated future change while preserving the verified user-list behavior and GitHub Pages delivery path.

in: Replace react-scripts development and production build commands with Vite
Preserve equivalent lint and non-interactive test commands
Keep all five existing behavioral tests passing or migrate them to an equivalent supported runner
Update GitHub Actions and GitHub Pages artifact handling from build/ to dist/
Remove Create React App-only entry points, dependencies, and generated assumptions
Preserve relative asset paths for the customer_hook repository Pages URL

acceptance_criteria: A clean lockfile installation supports local development, lint, tests, and a production Vite build.
The existing five behavioral tests continue to protect loading, results, errors, empty responses, search debounce, and no-match behavior.
The pull-request Quality gate passes with the migrated toolchain.
A successful push to main uploads dist/ and deploys the application to GitHub Pages.
The deployed customer_hook site loads its JavaScript, CSS, manifest, and public assets from valid repository-relative paths.
react-scripts and obsolete Create React App-only files and dependencies are removed.

checkpoints.summary: Confirm the Vite, test-runner, asset-path, and environment-variable migration design before implementation.
evidence: Deferred by the repository owner on 2026-08-14 because this is a large cross-cutting toolchain change

checkpoints.summary: Replace react-scripts and CRA entry points while preserving local development and production builds.
Preserve behavioral tests and update the Quality gate for the selected Vite-compatible test setup.
Deploy the Vite dist/ artifact to GitHub Pages without breaking repository-relative asset paths.

open_questions: Whether to migrate the existing Jest tests to Vitest or preserve Jest as a separate runner.
Whether future API configuration should use a required VITE_USERS_API_URL value or a documented DummyJSON default.
risks: The migration changes development, testing, production build, CI artifact, and deployment behavior at the same time.
Incorrect Vite base configuration can produce a successful build whose assets fail under the GitHub Pages repository path.
Changing the test runner can weaken behavioral coverage if assertions or browser-environment setup are lost during conversion.
Combining this migration with product changes would make regressions harder to isolate within the two-day assignment window.

deferral.reason: This is a large cross-cutting infrastructure change that affects local development, tests, production builds, CI, GitHub Pages artifacts, asset paths, and environment-variable conventions. It is intentionally outside the two-day assignment scope; the behavioral baseline and CI/CD pipeline now provide a safe foundation for a separate future migration.
deferral.revisit_when: After the current repository-readiness improvements are submitted and a dedicated migration scope is approved.

evidence: No migration code was implemented as part of the deferral decision.

human_review.notes: The repository owner explicitly chose to defer the Vite migration because its cross-cutting scope is too large for the current assignment window.
